stories.summary: OpenAI appoints Dan Driscoll to advise on responsible AI for national security modernization, cyber resilience, and collaboration with U.S. allies.

sources.title: OpenAI appoints Dan Driscoll as Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: OpenAI hires former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for national security role
sources.text: OpenAI has hired former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll as senior counselor for national security modernization, a newly created role at the company . Driscoll will focus on how artificial intelligence can be used to strengthen U.S. national security and cybersecurity, OpenAI said, while his updated LinkedIn profile also lists his new position. He will work with OpenAI's senior leadership and external partners, with a particular focus on helping U.S. allies adopt advanced AI responsibly. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the U.S. has "an extraordinary opportunity to work with other countries to spread the adoption of democratic AI," and that Driscoll's appointment would help strengthen American leadership in the technology. "National security requirements are changing faster than at any time in the past fifty years," Driscoll said. He added that AI could help reduce paperwork, process information and deliver answers more quickly to those working in national security. The appointment comes after Driscoll stepped down as Army secretary earlier this year after months of reported tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. An Iraq war veteran, Driscoll pushed efforts to modernize the U.S. military, including expanding access to drone and counter-drone technologies among U.S. allies, according to a previous U.S. Army announcement. Driscoll also met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv in November 2025 to discuss a U.S.-proposed peace plan aimed at ending the war with Russia, according to a statement from the Presidential Office of Ukraine. At OpenAI, Driscoll will work with government officials, industry leaders, academic institutions and allied organizations to advance what the company calls "democratic AI." He will also help internal teams understand the operational needs of national security institutions, building on OpenAI's efforts to strengthen cyber resilience and protect essential services through its Daybreak program .

sources.title: OpenAI wants to rebrand data centers as 'compute campuses' to try and win people over
sources.text: OpenAI is considering a new name for its biggest data centers as it looks to improve public perceptions of AI infrastructure amid ongoing political debate. Instead of calling them data centers, the ChatGPT maker is considering a rebrand to 'AI compute campuses' to give the facilities a name which sounds more economically positive. OpenAI hasn't directly announced these plans, however Axios reports that the changes could come as soon as this week, following US midterm elections on November 3 2026. It seems that the company is anticipating major political changes and the possibility that the Democrats regain control of the House of Representatives, which would result in a more challenging regulatory environment. OpenAI Chief Global Affairs Officer Chris Lehane told Axios that he expects AI to be an ongoing political debate beyond the midterm elections. "Communities should hold companies responsible and accountable so they really and truly get a transformative benefit from these projects," he added. OpenAI has already been making efforts to win communities over, promising to partner with local communities to understand local needs. "We commit to paying our own way on energy, so that our operations don't increase your electricity prices," the company said at the start of 2026. A May 2026 report revealed that US states could face energy price hikes of between 6% and 29% by the end of the decades, and the US is already on course to re-open disused nuclear facilities to keep up with demand. sources.name: The Verge AI
sources.title: OpenAI is quietly renaming data centers ‘compute campuses’
sources.text: Critics say OpenAI should tackle people’s concerns about data centers, not rebrand them. Critics say OpenAI should tackle people’s concerns about data centers, not rebrand them. People hate data centers . They’re loud, resource-hungry eyesores that are so profoundly unpopular they have managed to achieve the near-impossible in today’s polarized political landscape: genuine bipartisan opposition . But what about “compute campuses”? Those sound lovely, right? OpenAI seems to be gambling that a quiet rebrand could be all it takes to defuse the growing political backlash that threatens to derail the infrastructure fueling the AI boom. OpenAI debuted the new terminology on Monday in an announcement launching its new “Grid Protectors Program.” The initiative, starting with an upcoming site in Effingham County, Georgia, aims to address concerns about the strain its sprawling AI infrastructure places on local power grids, particularly during extreme weather and emergencies. It’s a familiar data center problem. Yet in the roughly 900-word announcement, the term “data center” appeared just twice, outnumbered by “compute campus.” The initiative addresses worries about electricity use and the prospect of consumers being left to foot the bill for the AI buildout. OpenAI promises to “pay the costs we create” and “help communities keep the lights on.” Its two mentions of “data center” reinforce the connection: One references US data center capacity and electricity consumption, while the other directly compares OpenAI’s new “compute facilities” with “data centers built even a few years ago.” They’re “much different,” OpenAI says, with the new campuses allowing the company to be rather vaguely “flexible in our power demand.” The terminology appears to be new for OpenAI. A quick search of its website turned up no previous uses of the term. The timing is noteworthy, too. On Monday, Axios reported that OpenAI was planning to rebrand data centers as “AI compute campuses” as part of a policy and PR push after Tuesday’s midterms, anticipating a more hostile regulatory environment if Democrats make gains. Apparently, the rebrand couldn’t wait. Critics, however, aren’t buying it. A new name does nothing to lessen data centers’ environmental footprint , ease the burdens they place on local resources, or address the concerns of nearby residents. Activist groups who spoke to The Verge see the rebrand as a fairly transparent attempt to break free from an increasingly toxic label without meaningfully tackling what made it toxic to begin with. It fits within a broader lobbying push by Big Tech to counter souring public sentiment. “OpenAI is clearly responding to the unpopularity of data centers,” said Holly Elmore, founder and executive director of PauseAI US, a grassroots group campaigning to pause AI development. “Rebranding them ‘compute campuses’ may fool listeners once or twice but it’s not the name ‘data center’ that is unpopular — it’s the giant, polluting construction projects that apparently threatened to turn off people’s heat in the winter,” Elmore told The Verge in an email, calling OpenAI’s electricity announcement “woefully tone deaf.” “Communities that despise them will not be fooled into thinking they have transformed into something else.” Abre’ Conner, director of the NAACP’s Center for Environmental and Climate Justice, was similarly unimpressed. “This feels like an empty solution to an existing issue, which is that the data center infrastructure causes real harm,” she told The Verge . “Changing the name does not fix the problem and makes it seem like people’s health and our environment are public relations problems not environmental and climate concerns.” Conner argued that OpenAI should focus on changing its practices rather than what it calls data centers. “At a time when companies could utilize their resources to develop new models, create more transparency, and slow the infrastructure development, their solution is to just change their name.” Elmore agreed, suggesting the data center rebrand was an attempt by OpenAI to keep up with its rival Anthropic, but that it isn’t “spinning it nearly as well.” Earlier this year, Anthropic pledged to cover 100 percent of the upgrades needed to connect its data centers to power grids, including those that would normally be passed on to consumers. The company has also promised to invest billions of dollars in community projects developed with local leaders, protect local water supplies, and refrain from asking public officials to sign NDAs — a practice that has recently come under scrutiny . Anthropic said those commitments apply to both leased and owned data centers. Leased facilities currently make up most of its infrastructure, though its recent S-1 filing ahead of its IPO indicates the company wants to aggressively build its own, too, with many relying on gas . OpenAI did not respond to The Verge’ s request for comment about its decision to change nomenclature, its motivations for doing so, or whether doing so is an attempt to distance itself from the growing controversy surrounding data centers.

stories.title: Elon Musk se ríe de Sam Altman por afirmar que es terrible que tu PC de casa tenga memoria RAM: "¡La gente se merece tener su RAM!"
stories.summary: La crisis de la RAM está dando mucho que hablar. Hasta el punto de que el CEO de Tesla ha decidido cargar contra el creador de ChatGPT por sus últimas declaraciones.

sources.name: Computer Hoy
sources.title: Elon Musk se ríe de Sam Altman por afirmar que es terrible que tu PC de casa tenga memoria RAM: "¡La gente se merece tener su RAM!"
sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. La crisis de la RAM está dando mucho que hablar. Hasta el punto de que el CEO de Tesla ha decidido cargar contra el creador de ChatGPT por sus últimas declaraciones. Ya no es noticia decir que los precios se han disparado y comprar un ordenador nuevo o mejorar el que ya tienes cuesta cada vez más . La memoria RAM es la parte más afectada y parece que ante esto Elon Musk, CEO de X, Tesla y SpaceX, tiene algo que decir al respecto y, sobre todo, contra algo con lo que no está de acuerdo y que ha comentado Sam Altman, CEO de OpenAI. Contextualizando, durante una entrevista en el canal de YouTube Cheeky Pint , Altman defendió que no tiene demasiado sentido que cada persona tenga grandes cantidades de memoria RAM en su ordenador si apenas las utiliza . Según su punto de vista, sería más eficiente que esa memoria estuviera en centros de datos y se aprovechara desde la nube. "Desde el punto de vista de la distribución global, es bastante terrible que todo el mundo tenga una gran cantidad de la limitada memoria DRAM del mundo en su propio ordenador y la utilice un 5% del tiempo", explicó Altman. Elon Musk no ha podido quedarse callado y se ha burlado de las palabras de Altman con un meme y un mensaje en X: "¡La gente se merece tener su RAM!". Lo cierto es que las palabras de Altman tienen cierto sentido y razón. Sin embargo, que esto venga de alguien que precisamente controla una de las mayores empresas de inteligencia artificial del mundo resulta bastante insultante. Actualmente, la situación es tan crítica y los precios están tan disparados por culpa de estas compañías . A los fabricantes de chips les resulta más rentable fabricar las RAM de los centros de datos de IA que las que se usan en PC de usuarios normales debido a las fortunas que les pagan. OpenAI, por supuesto, está en ellas. Fabricantes como Samsung y SK Hynix ya han comentado en varias ocasiones que los problemas de suministro podrían continuar durante 2027 y más allá . Lenovo también ha avisado de que no espera que los precios vuelvan pronto a los niveles anteriores a 2026. De ahí que resulte bastante ofensivo que ataque precisamente a estos usuarios que buscan tener un ordenador potente, por el que, por cierto, tienen que pagar más que el resto. Muchas personas ahora mismo se encuentran en una situación muy complicada : necesitan más memoria para sus ordenadores (le den un uso o no más eficiente), pero cada vez cuesta más conseguirla. Y mientras las grandes compañías de IA compiten por hacerse con los recursos para seguir creciendo a toda costa, el usuario base que solo quiere mejorar su PC tiene que pagar más. Sin ir más lejos, hace unos días Samsung volvió a recordar que la situación está lejos de estabilizarse . Tanto esta empresa como otras afirman que el sector se está dirigiendo totalmente hacia un cuello de botella estructural que va a perjudicar todo el sector tecnológico mucho más allá del año 2026 . Los centros de datos que utilizan empresas como las grandes tecnológicas necesitan cantidades enormes de memoria para entrenar y ejecutar sus modelos. Y los fabricantes están dedicando cada vez más recursos a producir los componentes que necesitan estas máquinas. El problema es que las fábricas no pueden aumentar su producción de un día para otro. Samsung ha confirmado que ya tiene cubierta toda su capacidad de suministro de HBM4 (la memoria para la IA) para 2027 . Sus clientes ya han reservado toda la producción que Samsung espera tener disponible para ese año. También ha explicado que prevé comenzar la producción en masa de la siguiente generación, HBM4E, durante la primera mitad de 2027, con un aumento de la producción durante la segunda mitad del año. Mientras tanto, Elon Musk se posiciona en el bando mayoritario, haciendo uso de las redes sociales, para hacer creer a la gente que está a su favor. Sin embargo, hay que recordar de quién estamos hablando y que, por supuesto, también está al frente de una gran compañía de IA. Pero el odio entre Elon Musk y Sam Altman lleva años dando que hablar. Aunque juntos fundaron OpenAI hace más de una década, ahora están en polos opuestos. El break point precisamente tuvo lugar por aquel entonces. A principios de 2018, dejó la empresa y Altman asumió el papel de CEO . El lanzamiento de ChatGPT en 2022 marcó un punto de inflexión. OpenAI, bajo la dirección de Altman, se hizo con toda la atención global con su modelo de lenguaje. Mientras que Musk, quien había abandonado la compañía, vio cómo su visión sobre la IA se hacía realidad sin él. Su respuesta fue lanzar xAI, una empresa destinada a competir con OpenAI . Sin embargo, sus avances están bastante lejos de igualar el impacto de ChatGPT. Al final, esto hace que su odio, poco a poco, no pare de crecer y cualquier excusa es buena para volver a dejarlo claro.

sources.title: 'The people deserve to have their RAM too!' Elon Musk mocks OpenAI Sam Altman's claim that people owning home PCs with RAM is 'terrible'
sources.text: Elon Musk has mocked OpenAI CEO Sam Altman following the latter's declaration that owning a PC with RAM is 'quite terrible' , as the components should be powering the next generation of AI data centers. In his typically irreverent manner, Musk shared a meme on X , the social network he owns, showing a version of a scene from Inglorious Basterds with a German WWII officer played by Christoph Waltz apparently hunting for people hiding sticks of DRAM. "The people deserve to have their RAM too!" Musk's meme declares. Altman made his claim during an appearance on the YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, with his beliefs causing widespread condemnation and confusion across the industry. "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time," Altman said. "You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that." Altman's comments come as consumers face rising prices for any kind of computing hardware as the demand for RAM and other components gets passed down. Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed! In recent months, we've seen the likes of Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan warning of continued shortages and price rises , noting, "AI hardware will stay in short supply for the next 2 to 3 years", a trend he said was "driven by persistent constraints in the underlying tech supply chain." Dell CEO Michael Dell has also voiced his belief that the memory shortage will get worse through 2027, and that these RAM woes are going to be prolonged for quite some time. Top DRAM manufacturers Samsung and SK hynix have also warned that AI-driven memory shortages will last until 2027 and beyond , with their supplies rumored to be down to fewer than 10 days of memory inventory. Interestingly, Altman reportedly recently met with about 50 senior Samsung executives in South Korea, as he looked to secure more hardware for OpenAI to expand its AI capacity. But no matter what happens, one thing that (probably) won't happen is Altman breaking into your house to steal your PC's RAM ...probably. stories.title: OpenAI vai ‘aposentar’ ChatGPT Classic no começo de 2027; veja o que muda
stories.summary: O app do ChatGPT para desktop testará a integração entre os modos chat e Work.

sources.name: Tecmundo
sources.title: OpenAI vai ‘aposentar’ ChatGPT Classic no começo de 2027; veja o que muda
sources.text: OpenAI encerra conta e alerta Polícia Federal sobre homem que planejou atentado contra Lula no ChatG Entenda a ação da OpenAI ao banir a conta de um usuário e acionar a Polícia Federal e o TSE após detectar planos de ataque contra o presidente Lula no ChatGPT. A OpenAI vai aposentar o ChatGPT Classic em 30 de janeiro de 2027. A data foi divulgada para usuários do antigo aplicativo. Ao mesmo tempo, a empresa prepara uma experiência unificada para o chatbot e o agente ChatGPT Work no programa mais recente. O ChatGPT Classic ganhou esse nome após a estreia da versão repaginada do aplicativo desktop em julho deste ano , que reunia o chat, o ChatGPT Work e o Codex em uma única interface. Na época, a OpenAI buscava ampliar o acesso às ferramentas de inteligência artificial agênticas. O ChatGPT Classic, por sua vez, continuou oferecendo uma experiência semelhante à do ChatGPT disponível na web, com histórico de conversas, biblioteca, projetos e outros recursos de texto. Com o passar dos meses, o aplicativo ficou defasado em relação à nova versão, que recebia funcionalidades inéditas , como a capacidade de selecionar o nível de esforço de raciocínio. “Este aplicativo será desativado em 30 de janeiro de 2027. Acesse os recursos mais recentes no novo aplicativo do ChatGPT. Todo o seu histórico de conversas será transferido para que você possa continuar de onde parou”, diz o aviso encaminhado aos usuários. Dentro do novo app ChatGPT Desktop, a OpenAI prepara uma experiência de uso que reúne o chatbot e o Work em um só ambiente . A mudança torna a linha entre as conversas puramente por texto e as funções agênticas mais tênue, poupando o usuário de escolher entre um modo ou outro. A integração entre agentes e chatbots segue uma tendência de mercado entre as gigantes provedoras de IA . Pouco a pouco, Google e Anthropic também aproximaram as experiências de chat e agente de IA, às vezes reduzindo a escolha a um simples interruptor na tela. A grande diferença entre um chatbot convencional e um agente como o ChatGPT Work é a autonomia para a execução de tarefas. Enquanto o chat é voltado principalmente à interação com o usuário, o Work pode assumir tarefas mais complexas, utilizar ferramentas e executar diferentes etapas sob orientação humana. O teste começará com um pequeno grupo de pessoas , segundo um e-mail enviado pela OpenAI. “A mudança permitirá que você leve a exploração de uma ideia para a execução no ChatGPT, tudo em um só lugar. Você pode trazer seus arquivos e plugins e pedir o ChatGPT para construir um site, criar uma apresentação, ou fazer coisas por você na web, enquanto revisa e orienta seu trabalho. O Codex continuará uma experiência distinta dentro do app ChatGPT Desktop”. Junto com a transição, a OpenAI também planeja implementar uma franquia de uso compartilhada entre o ChatGPT e o Codex , substituindo os limites separados. A novidade está prevista para dezembro de 2026 nos planos Plus, Pro e Business. Segundo a companhia, a mudança não deve fazer com que a maioria dos usuários precise esperar pela renovação dos limites com mais frequência. O consumo será calculado conforme o modelo utilizado e a complexidade da tarefa. As conversas ilimitadas no modo “Instant” continuarão incluídas nos planos contemplados e não consumirão a franquia compartilhada. Quer ficar por dentro das novidades do mundo da tecnologia? sources.title: OpenAI vai unificar limites do ChatGPT e Codex; veja o que muda
sources.text: A OpenAI vai unificar os limites de uso do ChatGPT e do Codex a partir de dezembro, mas a empresa ainda não divulgou o dia exato em que a alteração entrará em vigor. A mudança afetará os assinantes dos planos Plus, Pro e Business. Segundo a OpenAI, a novidade acompanha a integração dos recursos de inteligência artificial agêntica do Work à experiência principal do ChatGPT. Com o novo modelo, o consumo será calculado em tokens , unidades de informação processadas pelos modelos de IA. O gasto dependerá do modelo escolhido e da complexidade de cada tarefa. Assim, solicitações mais exigentes vão consumir uma parcela maior da cota. A mudança também terá impacto no uso combinado das duas ferramentas. Uma longa sessão de programação no Codex, por exemplo, reduzirá o limite disponível para tarefas complexas no ChatGPT. O mesmo vale no sentido contrário. A exceção fica por conta das conversas no Instant chat , que não descontarão tokens da cota compartilhada. Até então, ChatGPT, Work e Codex tinham limites independentes , com cotas próprias para envio de arquivos, geração de imagens e interações por voz. Os assinantes do Plus também contavam com uma janela de uso de cinco horas para o Codex e o Work e uma cota semanal. A nova estrutura vai concentrar o consumo dos serviços em um único limite. Quando a cota acabar, os usuários terão três alternativas : aguardar a renovação do limite, fazer upgrade do plano ou comprar créditos adicionais para continuar usando os recursos. A OpenAI também vai mostrar o saldo restante e o tempo estimado até a próxima renovação no menu “Configurações” > “Uso”. A OpenAI afirma que está preparando a transição para evitar interrupções nos fluxos de trabalho. A expectativa é que a maioria dos usuários mantenha uma frequência de renovação de limites semelhante à atual. A estratégia também acompanha uma mudança adotada pela Anthropic , que unificou as cotas do Claude para o chat, o Cowork e o Claude Code . A documentação da OpenAI ainda não informa qual será o volume de tokens disponível em cada plano . Também faltam detalhes sobre a frequência de renovação dos limites e possíveis mudanças nas regras de uso. Outro ponto em aberto é o impacto da novidade nas assinaturas Free e Go . Até o momento, a empresa não confirmou se esses planos também terão alterações na contabilização do consumo. Se você gostou do texto, talvez também se interesse por conferir “ ChatGPT Codex e Claude Code: o que muda entre as IAs para programação? ”.

sources.name: The Verge AI
sources.title: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
sources.text: ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI. ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI. In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google. Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how-to explanation. (Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.) Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade. During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree. (OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant part of its searches, along with its in-house search index, although there is still some speculation that it routes some queries through Google.) The news comes amid an ongoing search engine shake-up, as Google continues to reduce conventional referrals to third-party sites and invests heavily in AI tools — not just AI Overview but also additional generative AI capabilities , including personalized search results with visualizations and charts. But as search queries increasingly route through OpenAI and other AI labs’ services, other companies are investing in the same types of AI-focused search experience, even if they call it something else: for OpenAI, it’s “Intelligent UI,” or creating a visual and interactive interface within a chatbot response. “That’s where the future of this technology goes. You’re talking to a canvas,” Fry said. Much like Google, OpenAI sees a potential path to profitability through ads, particularly as it approaches an IPO potentially slated for early next year. OpenAI has defended its ads in the past, and Fry told reporters they hadn’t produced a lasting backlash. “Ads have not negatively impacted the product or the usage of the product,” he said, adding that “most people do not seem to mind ads in the product.” OpenAI announced last month that the company would begin introducing images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT rather than just a company’s name, logo, and a link to its product like before. “Ads have maybe shown us that we could be doing this more, actually,” Fry said.
